summary_hint: Tells a processor whose IRS-sourced 1099 income record this is, for which year, and how many payer records it contains.

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity — confirms this is an IRS transcript vs a borrower-provided 1099

typed_core.name: transcript_type
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — 'Wage & Income' vs other transcript types (degraded from enum)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture transcript_type verbatim ('Wage and Income Transcript'); the 1099 records are a subset

typed_core.name: transcript_request_or_run_date
typed_core.why: recency — when the transcript was pulled

typed_core.name: tax_year
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — the year the records belong to; a record amount is meaningless without its year
typed_core.prompt_hint: tax_year at the header applies to every record and must accompany any amount downstream

typed_core.name: recipient_name
typed_core.why: identity — the taxpayer; match to borrower (degraded from person_or_entity)

typed_core.name: recipient_tin_masked
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted); identity — the TIN the records are filed under
typed_core.prompt_hint: TINs masked as XXX-XX-1234; retain last-4. Never emit to the catch-all

typed_core.name: address_or_customer_file_number
typed_core.why: processor/matching — customer file number or address used to order the transcript

nested_lists.name: information_return_records
nested_lists.shape_reason: the 1099 records are the document's payload and genuinely repeat (a few to ~20 payers); flat rows with one source each are token-safe and let a processor reconcile line-by-line

fields.name: payer_name
fields.why: reconciliation — the payer that reported the income

fields.name: payer_tin_masked
fields.why: identity of the payer within the record
fields.pii_note: PII (registry has payer_tin masked) — the nested list needs its own redactor, not the raw catch-all

fields.name: box_or_income_type
fields.why: reconciliation — the box/income-type; the same dollar figure means different things by box

fields.name: amount
fields.why: reconciliation — the reported amount (whole-dollar on transcripts)

fields.name: account_number_masked
fields.pii_note: PII (registered) — the nested list needs its own redactor so it is masked, not stored raw in a catch-all

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: a transcript is not a numbered form

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start/_end, document_issue_date
rejected.reason: not applicable; transcript_request_or_run_date + tax_year cover timing

rejected.name: aggregate_amounts_by_form_and_box (TECHNICAL)
rejected.reason: a computed conclusion, not a fact — summing is a rule's job; tags describe, rules judge

rejected.name: missing_or_unmatched_payer_records (TECHNICAL)
rejected.reason: a reconciliation finding/judgment — produced by comparing against borrower 1099s, not read from this document

encoding_variations: Transcript type printed as 'Wage and Income Transcript'; the 1099 records are a subset — capture transcript_type verbatim

Each record's form is labeled by IRS form code (1099-NEC, 1099-MISC, 1099-INT, 1099-DIV, 1099-R, 1099-G, 1099-K) with box numbers — capture the form code AND the box/income-type together, because the same dollar figure means different things by box
Amounts are whole-dollar on transcripts; retain as printed
TINs masked as XXX-XX-1234 / XX-XXX1234; retain last-4

open_questions.q: information_return_records column set. Recommended flat-row columns: form_type, payer_name, payer_tin_masked, box/income_type, amount, account_number_masked.
options: finer box granularity (some transcripts print multiple boxes per record)
open_questions.recommendation: confirm the box/income-type granularity is sufficient (some transcripts print multiple boxes per record)

open_questions.q: Masked-TIN registration. recipient_tin_masked and nested payer_tin_masked are masked variants not literally in the 7-field registry.
options: register the masked field names (pre_masked true)
rely on the raw-name registry entries
open_questions.recommendation: register the masked field names (pre_masked true); confirm the registry keys on exact field name

open_questions.q: Recipient could be an entity. recipient_name is person_or_entity; flattened to str.
open_questions.recommendation: confirm no downstream needs a person-vs-entity flag (relevant for business 1099 income)

notes: This is an IRS-sourced record (authoritative), distinct from borrower-provided 1099s — one transcript can list many payers.
Capture each record's IRS form code and box number together; tax_year at the header applies to every record and must accompany any amount downstream.
Do not aggregate or reconcile — emit each payer record as-is; totals and unmatched-payer findings are a rule's job, not the extractor's.
recipient_tin_masked needs _PII_FIELDS registration, pre_masked true (the transcript already masks it); the registry lists recipient_tin raw, not the masked variant.
Within information_return_records, payer_tin_masked and account_number_masked are PII — the nested list needs its own redactor so these are masked, not stored raw in a catch-all.
